messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — alert: realtime-streaming p99 latency spike > 3x baseline for 5m, error-rate up 1.8%. Affected route: /v1/stream/generate (model variants: gpt-small-int8-v2, gpt-small-fp8-v1). Runbook: https://runbook.internal/realtime/streaming-latency. Priority: P1.
Sara_oncall: acked. jumping in. any recent deploys or calib rollouts?
Mike_sre: I see a background rollout of quant calib `calib/v2.3-int8` to canary yesterday that started ramping at 02:12 UTC. pinned to 10% then auto-ramped.
Elaine_prod: customer CS reporting websocket resets for a few enterprise customers, one flow shows repeated `stall` events during long streaming (~2k tokens).
Sara_oncall: copying graphs from infra dashboard — p95 up 1.3x, p99 up 3.4x, tail > 10s on some requests. CPU on gpu-nodes stable, but KV cache miss ratio jumped, and stream worker queue length spiked.
Mike_sre: KV contention + increased cache misses lines up with quant calibration fallout we've seen when int8 profile underestimates activation ranges. leads to extra dequant/decode steps and async stalls.
Chris_cs: which customers impacted? need to notify.
Elaine_prod: two paying accounts on dedicated capacity (acct-589, acct-221) reported degraded UX; small percentage of requests got 502/connection-reset. non-critical overall but potential SLA exposure.
Sara_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop calib ramp (freeze) 2) route streaming to high-precision fallback for affected traffic 3) if routing change not enough, rollback calib profile to previous `calib/v2.2`.
Sara_oncall: Mike, can you flip router weights for streaming route to prefer `gpt-small-fp16-stable` for steady traffic and keep int8 as fallback? quick CLI:
```
# temporarily prioritize fp16 for streaming
radmin set-route-weight --route /v1/stream/generate --model gpt-small-fp16-stable --weight 0.9
radmin set-route-weight --route /v1/stream/generate --model gpt-small-int8-v2 --weight 0.1
```
Mike_sre: applying now. will monitor p99.
deploy-bot: executing change: `radmin set-route-weight ...` — done (change-id: ch_20260315_01).
infra-bot: router config propagated to us-east-1/us-west-2.
Sara_oncall: also flipping the calibration rollout gate to pause canary on control plane:
```
# pause calib rollout
calibctl rollback --profile calib/v2.3-int8 --target canary
```
Mike_sre: ran the pause. control-plane shows canary halted and no further ramp.
Sara_oncall: Observability: p95 back within 1.05x baseline in 90s, p99 trending down. KV miss ratio decreasing. :white_check_mark:
Chris_cs: I'll draft a short customer note: "We've applied a routing fix to reduce latency and paused a calibration rollout; your traffic should be stable. We'll follow up with details and RCA."
Elaine_prod: one more mitigation option if we see edge cases: enable streaming chunk-level fallback—send partial responses from FP16 branch for long contexts. that's longer change though.
Mike_sre: FYI I opened an incident ticket and annotated the change ids + telemetry: INC-2419. Adding trace IDs for affected requests.
Sara_oncall: handoff: Mike will continue mitigation and dig into why `calib/v2.3-int8` produced KV miss pattern. I'm stepping off in 20m — @mike_sre please escalate to eng-runtime if we see repeat spikes.
Mike_sre: noted. I'll correlate activation histograms with quant thresholds, and check quantization tool output for out-of-range activations. Evidence so far suggests a drift in sequence-length distribution on streaming requests combined with a calibration snapshot that assumed shorter sequences.
Sara_oncall: tagging follow-ups for postmortem: - why canary ramped despite KV miss heuristics? - add rollback automation to routing runbook - validate calib tool against long-context traces - customer communication timeline.
deploy-bot: rollback completed for calib/v2.3-int8 to `calib/v2.2` on canary (op-id: rb_2419994321).
Mike_sre: after rollback, p99 stabilized to 1.02x baseline, error-rate back to normal. leaving monitoring on for 1h.
Elaine_prod: CS update sent to affected accounts, flagged as incident under review.
Chris_cs: customers acknowledged and appreciate the quick notice. no escalation request yet.
Mike_sre: next steps: collect sample traces, run offline calibration with extended sequences, and create a synthetic load sim for long streaming contexts to catch regressions. I'll schedule a gating test in CI that exercises 2k+ token sequences for quant profiles.
Sara_oncall: thanks team. I'll file the postmortem and schedule a 30m debrief tomorrow. closing paging channel in 10. :lock:
incident-bot: incident status updated to `mitigated`. responders: sara_oncall, mike_sre, elaine_prod, chris_cs.
_note: This file represents a single Slack thread; messages are a continuous string with sender prefixes per agents.md
